name: Montenegro
headline: Montenegro: +2.7% growth in 2025, 3.9% inflation, debt 64% of GDP
sections: Montenegro is a $9.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 157th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.7% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $35K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 3.3% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 3.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 13.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 13.6% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 24.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 64% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 106% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.3% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −20.6% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 106% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 7.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 65% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.9 years (2024). Population: 624 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
